rulings.challenge_claim: The closing verse is characterised as carrying a covenant curse although the curse lexeme reaches MT 11:3 and not MT 11:8 (skeleton sweep: 5 verses book-wide); the covenant-words catchword crossing the opening seam is undisclosed; and the closing-seam assertion that MT 11:9 opens with the same introduction again carries no splice and no tier, the two forms being skeleton-identical but not byte-identical.
rulings.grounds: All three limbs verify on the bytes. MT 11:8 closes וָאָבִ֨יא עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶֽת כָּל דִּבְרֵ֧י הַבְּרִית הַזֹּ֛את (oshb:Jer.11.8, byte) — the covenant-words object — and carries no curse lexeme anywhere in the verse; אָר֣וּר stands at oshb:Jer.11.3 (byte), outside the span and uncited, the run occurring in 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton) and only there in this chapter. The covenant-words construct chain occurs in 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton), four of them in this chapter at 11:2, 11:3, 11:6 and 11:8, so a byte-true catchword straddles the unit's own front seam while the disclosure sentence names only the two segs — a straddling device argues continuity unless disclosed. The recurrence limb holds too: the onset splice וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.11.6, byte) collates at byte tier at its cited ref, while the same run at oshb:Jer.11.9 reads וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.11.9, byte) in pausal pointing — skeleton-identical, not byte-identical (sweep: 13 verses, skeleton) — and the closing-seam sentence asserts the sameness with neither splice nor tier. The cut itself is untouched: the fresh introduction at 11:9 and the setumah at oshb:Jer.11.8 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3) both stand, so these are citation and disclosure defects, not a boundary defect.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the covenant-curse characterisation of the closing verse with the covenant-words object actually standing in it, spliced from source bytes with its oshb ref and tier; if the curse is to be argued at all, splice it at oshb:Jer.11.3 with its tier and add web:Jer.11.3 to boundary_evidence_refs, since it would then be argued outside the span. boundary_rationale: splice the introduction at oshb:Jer.11.9 with its ref and tier and state the recurrence against oshb:Jer.11.6 as skeleton-identical, not byte-identical. device_notes: disclose the covenant-words construct chain crossing the 11:5|11:6 front seam (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton; four in this chapter) and why it does not defeat the cut — the same straddle faces the seam from both sides, so it is one edit, not two. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: no curse lexeme anywhere in 11:8's bytes; the two introduction forms re-collated separately at byte tier; every recurrence sentence carrying its tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: The discriminator separating this unit from what precedes — a turn to the present generation's conspiracy rather than the fathers' history just recalled — is contradicted by this unit's own second verse, which names the forefathers twice; and the speech formula at MT 11:11, on which the refusal to cut turns, is left unspliced.
rulings.grounds: The formula limb is upheld and the contrast limb needs correction. Upheld: the unit's only Hebrew splice sits at its opening, and לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.11.11, byte) — the form on which both the internal-seam refusal and the rejected alternative rest — is quoted nowhere and carries no tier; the prose also calls it a koh-amar clause without naming the therefore-particle prefixing it, so it is not the unbridged verse-initial shape. Corrected: the fathers are not this span's subject. שָׁ֩בוּ֩ עַל עֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתָ֜ם הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.11.10, byte) opens with a finite verb whose subject is the conspiring men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem named at the onset, with the forefathers standing as the owners of the iniquities returned to and as the covenant partners — so the subject contrast the seam rests on survives the bytes and the challenge overstates it. What the bytes do establish is a disclosure debt: the fathers-noun with its suffixes recurs in 4 verses of this chapter (sweep: 44 verses book-wide on the consonantal run, skeleton), at 11:4, 11:5 and 11:7 before the seam and 11:10 inside it, an undisclosed byte-true catchword across the unit's own front seam. Both edges otherwise hold, corroborated by the setumah at oshb:Jer.11.8 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3).
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the therefore-prefixed formula from oshb:Jer.11.11 with its ref and tier, naming the particle so the form is not read as an unbridged verse-initial onset; strongest_rejected_alternative, which turns on the same form, inherits that splice. boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: qualify the contrast to the change of grammatical subject at the onset rather than to the disappearance of the fathers. device_notes: disclose the fathers-noun run crossing the front seam (sweep: 44 verses book-wide, skeleton; 11:4, 11:5, 11:7 and 11:10 in this chapter) and why it does not defeat the cut. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: the two forefather tokens inside 11:10 accounted for in the unit's own prose, and every formula the rejected alternative depends on carrying a byte-tier splice at its own oshb ref.

rulings.challenge_claim: The link holding MT 11:16 and MT 11:17 together is mis-described as a planting in 11:16 although the planting participle occurs at MT 11:17 (skeleton sweep: 1 verse in the book), and the recorded signal labels a prohibition an imperative.
rulings.grounds: Both limbs verify. The participle הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ stands at oshb:Jer.11.17 (byte) and occurs in exactly one verse in the book (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton), while oshb:Jer.11.16 carries no form of that root at all — its predicate is קָרָ֥א יְהוָ֖ה שְׁמֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.11.16, byte) — so the prose locates an act at a verse whose bytes do not carry it. The binding the argument reaches for is nonetheless real and runs through the second-person feminine chain the unit's own splice already displays: שְׁמֵ֑ךְ at oshb:Jer.11.16 (byte) picked up by הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ and עָלַ֖יִךְ at oshb:Jer.11.17 (byte). The form-class limb holds as well: אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ (oshb:Jer.11.14, byte) is the negative particle with a tav-prefixed prefix-conjugation form (sweep: 3 verses on that run, skeleton), whereas this stem's imperative shape is he-initial and stands in 5 verses elsewhere (sweep: 5 verses, skeleton), at none of them here; both witnesses render a prohibition (web:Jer.11.14), and the unit's own prose says prohibition while its recorded signal says discourse-imperative onset — a form-class label is a byte-checkable claim. Marks and seams are clean: the segs across the span's MT keys at oshb:Jer.11.14 and oshb:Jer.11.17 are both disclosed and correctly typed setumah (WLC, single-witness, tier-3).
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the discourse-imperative-onset key with a prohibition/vetitive key agreeing with the form in the bytes and with the unit's own prose. boundary_rationale: re-word the 11:16-11:17 link to the second-person feminine chain the splices already carry, leaving the planting participle at the verse that has it. boundary_rationale, same field, a further defect found here: the opening pairing sets the splice at oshb:Jer.11.14 against a WEB clause (web:Jer.11.14) whose leading connective renders nothing in the spliced run — that verse carries no therefore-particle — and which also runs past the splice to the prepositional object; re-cut gloss extent to splice extent. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: no form of the planting root anywhere in 11:16's bytes; the recorded signal key agreeing with the attested form; each quoted English clause rendering exactly the run spliced beside it.

rulings.challenge_claim: The statement that nothing before this verse is cast in this voice is refuted by the first-person chain closing MT 11:5 and again by MT 10:19-24, and the exclusivity names no swept object and carries no digit; separately, the closing Yahweh-of-Armies claim rests on MT 11:20, which is left unspliced, so the recorded divine-title signal has no quoted form behind it.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on the bytes. MT 11:5 closes וָאַ֥עַן וָאֹמַ֖ר אָמֵ֥ן יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.11.5, byte) — the prophet's own first-person report, thirteen verses before the verse said to introduce that voice and inside the same parent — and both witnesses render it as his own speech (web:Jer.11.5). Earlier still, וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי stands at oshb:Jer.10.19 (byte) and first-person petition runs at oshb:Jer.10.23 and oshb:Jer.10.24 (byte). The onset sentence states its exclusivity without qualification, without naming a swept object and without a digit, and an exclusivity of that shape is never dampened by the tier of the splice standing beside it. The second limb holds as well: וַֽיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ at oshb:Jer.11.20 (byte) is byte-true but unquoted, leaving the unit's recorded divine-title signal with no quoted form behind it. The onset itself is untouched — 11:18 does open a first-person report after divine speech closes at 11:17, corroborated by the setumah at oshb:Jer.11.17 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3) — so the defect lies in the warrant, not in the boundary.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the unqualified exclusivity, or bind it to a named swept object with a digit and a unit; if a first-occurrence reading is retained, disclose the first-person reply closing 11:5 and the petition voice at 10:19 and 10:23-10:24, and add web:Jer.11.5, web:Jer.10.19 and web:Jer.10.23-Jer.10.24 to boundary_evidence_refs, since they would then be argued outside the span. boundary_rationale or device_notes: splice the divine title from oshb:Jer.11.20 with its ref and tier so the recorded signal has a quoted form. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: 11:5's first-person report and the 10:19 and 10:23-10:24 petition forms all stand in the prophet's own voice, so any surviving first-occurrence sentence must exclude them by a named object; and every recorded signal must be anchored to a byte-tier splice at its own ref.

rulings.challenge_claim: The English set against the MT 11:22 splice renders a different clause of the verse than the spliced form, and the two therefore-clauses are treated as one object although they are distinct census objects, cited as sweeps of 152 and 50 verses.
rulings.grounds: The gloss limb is upheld and the count limb needs re-scoping. Upheld: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte) collates at byte tier at its cited ref, but the English paired with it in the same breath renders הַבַּֽחוּרִים֙ יָמֻ֣תוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב (oshb:Jer.11.22, byte), a later clause of the same verse; the clause that actually renders the spliced run is the therefore-Yahweh-of-Armies-says clause the pairing skips (web:Jer.11.22), so gloss extent and splice extent do not match and a byte-verified form is presented as saying something it does not say. Re-scoped: the two digits are not two disjoint objects. The tsevaot-expanded set (sweep: 50 verses, skeleton) is a proper subset of the koh-amar-YHWH set (sweep: 152 verses, skeleton) — 11:22 is counted in both, 11:21 in the larger set only — so the 152 figure is not the count of the without-tsevaot object and cannot be set against the 50 as a separate one. The substantive point survives that correction: the prose calls the second clause a further therefore-thus-says-Yahweh clause carrying the same speaker forward and never names the tsevaot expansion, which is the byte difference between לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte) and the clause at oshb:Jer.11.22, and the unit's recorded signals carry the plain speech formula while that divine-title stack goes unrecorded.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss so the English paired with the oshb:Jer.11.22 splice is the clause that renders it (web:Jer.11.22), or extend the splice to the clause the English renders; in the same field re-cut the oshb:Jer.11.21 pairing as well, whose gloss runs past the splice to the seek-your-life clause — a second extent mismatch found here. boundary_rationale: name the tsevaot expansion as the byte difference between the two therefore-clauses, giving each object its own digit and stating the containment (sweep: 152 verses and 50 verses, skeleton; the second inside the first). observed_substrate_signals: add the divine-title entry for the tsevaot stack standing at 11:22. The cure must pass the checks that killed the original: every quoted English clause rendering exactly the run spliced beside it, and any digit named beside a with- or without-tsevaot description stating which set it counts.
